messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problem with recursive formula for a Markov Chin Model
parts:
Usually you get NaN because you are trying to use a local variable
or transformed parameter before it is defined. We need to rewrite
those error messages, but I'm guessing B[1] here refers to the first
element of the second argument to multiply, P_transformed, the definition
for which you have commented out.

- Bob


> On Jan 9, 2017, at 11:02 AM, Elaheh Torkashvand <torkas...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Stan users,
>
> I am writing a code in stan to analyze my data. In the model I consider, there exists a Markov chain model. Please find the below for my code.
>
> stanmodelcode = " data {
> int<lower=1> N; // number of observed points for an experiment. Note that here I consider all trajectories in terms of their positions. The reason is the initial regression analysis shows that the cell position is explained by the covariates.
> int<lower=1> J; // number of trajectories.
> int<lower=1> D; // D refers to dimension
> int<lower=1> K; // number of states
> matrix[N, D] trajectory; // cartesian coordinates of positions in time.
> vector<lower=0>[D] alpha; // dirichlet distribution parameters
> vector[D] mu_b; // mean of random effects
> int<lower=1> counter_n[J]; // where to start the markovian process
> int<lower=1> b_final_f[J]; // where to end the markovian process
> int<lower=1> a_initial_f[J]; // first position of each trajectory
> matrix[N, 2] covariate; // There are two covariates available in this study.
> }
> parameters {
> vector[D] b[J]; // random effects.
> corr_matrix[D] Omega_b; // correlation matrix for random effects.
> vector<lower=0>[D] sigma_b; // scales parameters for random effects.
> vector[K] tau[D]; // similar to Joel paper.
> vector[K] beta[D]; // we have two covariates in the study and a vector of one.
> corr_matrix[D] Omega[K]; // correlation matrix
> simplex[K] prior_pi[J]; // k is the number of observed models we consider.
> simplex[K] P[K]; // transition matrix
> vector<lower=0>[D] sigma_error[K]; // to model error of X, Y, Z variables.
> }
>
> transformed parameters {
> matrix[K, K] P_transformed; //saving P as a matrix format.
> real<lower=0> nu;
> vector[D] b_rep[N];
> // random effects
> cov_matrix[D] Sigma_model_b; // I chose 3 as because of the cartisian coordinate setups.
> cov_matrix[D] Sigma_model[K]; // I chose 3 as because of the cartisian coordinate setups.
> nu =N-1;
> for (m in 1:D)
>
> Sigma_model_b[m,m] = sigma_b[m] * sigma_b[m] * Omega_b[m,m];
> for (m in 1:(D-1)) {
>
> for (n in (m+1):D) {
>
> Sigma_model_b[m,n] = sigma_b[m] * sigma_b[n] * Omega_b[m,n];
>
> Sigma_model_b[n,m] = Sigma_model_b[m,n];
> }
> }
> for(k in 1:K){
>
> for (d in 1:D){
>
> Sigma_model[k, d, d] = sigma_error[k, d] * sigma_error[k, d] * Omega[k, d, d];
> }
> for (m in 1:(D-1)) {
>
> for (n in (m+1):D) {
>
> Sigma_model[k, m, n] = sigma_error[k, m] * sigma_error[k, n] * Omega[k, m, n];
>
> Sigma_model[k, n, m] = Sigma_model[k, m, n];
> }
> }
>
> }
> for(j in 1:J){
> for(n in a_initial_f[j]: b_final_f[j]){
> b_rep[n]=b[j];
> }
>
> }
>
> # # # for(m in 1:K){
> # # # for(n in 1:K){
> # # # P_transformed[m, n] = P[m, n];
> # # # }
> # # # }
> }
> model {
> vector[K] prior_pi_alternative[N];
> matrix[K, N] models; // coordinates
> row_vector[K] a;
> matrix[N, D] mu_model[K]; // For now, I consider three states available in the study. Each element of the mu_model is considered a vector for K hidden states.
> for(k in 1:K)
> P[k] ~ dirichlet(alpha);
> for(j in 1:J){
> prior_pi[a_initial_f[j]] ~ dirichlet(alpha);
> prior_pi_alternative[a_initial_f[j]] = prior_pi[a_initial_f[j]];
> for(l in counter_n[j]: b_final_f[j]){
> a = prior_pi_alternative[l-1]' * P_transformed;
> prior_pi_alternative[l] = a';
> }
> }
> sigma_b ~ cauchy(0,5); // half-Cauchy due to constraint
> for(k in 1:K){
> sigma_error[k] ~ cauchy(0,5); // half-Cauchy due to constraint
> }
> # sigma_3 ~ cauchy(0,5); // half-Cauchy due to constraint
> Omega_b ~ lkj_corr(2.0); // regularize to unit correlation
> for(k in 1:K){
> Omega[k] ~ lkj_corr(2.0); // regularize to unit correlation
> }
>
> // Introducing no priors means we consider flat prior for the parameter. Note that the domain of the flat prior comes from the bound we have already defined for parameters.
> for(j in 1:J) {
> b[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_b, Sigma_model_b);
> }
> for(n in 1:N){
> for( d in 1:D){
> mu_model[1, n, d] = tau[d, 1]+beta[d, 1]+beta[d, 2]*covariate[n, 1]+beta[d, 3]*covariate[n, 2]+ b_rep[n, d];
> mu_model[2, n, d] = tau[d, 1]+tau[d, 2]+beta[d, 1]+beta[d, 2]*covariate[n, 1]+beta[d, 3]*covariate[n, 2]+ b_rep[n, d];
> mu_model[3, n, d] = tau[d, 1]+tau[d, 2]+tau[d, 3]+beta[d, 1]+beta[d, 2]*covariate[n, 1]+beta[d, 3]*covariate[n, 2]+ b_rep[n, d];
> }
>
> }
> for(n in 1:N) {
> for(k in 1:K){
> models[k, n] = log(prior_pi[n, k]) + multi_normal_lpdf(trajectory[n] | mu_model[k, n], Sigma_model[k]);
> }
> }
> for (k in 1:K)
> increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(models[k]));
> }
> "
>
>
> When I call stan for this model, the following model is generated
>
> " Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."
> [583] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"
> [584] "Exception thrown at line 87: multiply: B[1] is nan, but must not be nan!"
> [585] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
> [586] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."
>
>
> This error message is referring to
>
> a = prior_pi_alternative[l-1]' * P_transformed;
>
> Wonder if someone could help me figure out what is going wrong.
>
> Regards,
> Elaheh
